fact: Dirk Nowitzki stood 7'0" (84 inches) - nearly as tall as Shaquille O'Neal (7'1", 85 inches) - but shot 38.0% from three for his career, worlds ahead of Shaq's 4.5% (Shaq made exactly one three-pointer in 22 career attempts). Dirk even out-shot Muggsy Bogues, the shortest player in NBA history at 5'3", who hit 27.8% from deep. Reggie Miller (6'7", 39.5%) is the archetype pure sharpshooter - and Dirk, nearly half a foot taller, wasn't far behind him at all.
source: StatMuse / Basketball-Reference height and career 3-point percentage.

fact: Lou Williams built a three-time Sixth Man of the Year career on 24.1 minutes a game — barely two-thirds of Kobe Bryant's 36.1-minute workload — while still averaging 13.9 points, close to a full starter's production squeezed into a bench role. Manu Ginobili (25.4 MPG, 13.3 PPG) landed in almost the exact same zone despite a Hall-of-Fame resume, deployed off the bench by design for most of his prime. DeMar DeRozan (34.5 MPG, 21.1 PPG) shows the traditional high-usage starter workload both bench legends were compared against, not with.
source: StatMuse career per-game averages (regular season).

fact: Draymond Green scores less than half of what Klay Thompson does (8.7 PPG to 18.6) but combines for more rebounds and assists (12.4 to Klay's 5.6) — real proof a player can be a genuine star without scoring like one. Russell Westbrook (20.9 PPG, 14.9 combined) shows what happens when high scoring and stat-stuffing coexist, and Nikola Jokic (22.2 PPG, 18.6 combined) is the current extreme: elite at both at once, a center who also leads the league in rebounds and assists.
source: StatMuse career per-game averages (regular season).

fact: Jameis Winston throws touchdowns at almost the same rate as Brett Favre (4.8% vs. 5.0%) — but his interception rate (3.5%) is even higher than Favre's, the quarterback whose whole reputation is built on high-risk gunslinging. Alex Smith (2.1% / 3.8%) is the pure game-manager opposite: low risk, low reward. Aaron Rodgers (1.4% / 6.0%) shows the tradeoff isn't actually mandatory — the best touchdown rate in this set paired with the best career interception percentage in NFL history.
source: StatMuse career passing touchdown percentage and interception percentage.

fact: Zach Randolph made just 2 All-Star teams in his career — yet his 16.6 career points per game is basically identical to Joe Johnson's 16.0 (7 All-Star nods) and Vince Carter's 16.7 (8 nods). All-Star selections reward more than raw scoring average — team success, era, and position all factor in — and Randolph's Memphis grit-and-grind identity earned him far less recognition than his actual production. Karl Malone (14 AS, 25.0 PPG) anchors the other extreme: a player whose selections actually matched his all-time-great scoring.
source: StatMuse career per-game averages and career All-Star selection counts.

fact: Anquan Boldin made only 3 Pro Bowls in his career, but his 13,779 receiving yards is within shouting distance of Randy Moss's 15,292 — a player who made twice as many Pro Bowls. Boldin's game was built on contested catches and physicality rather than the highlight-reel speed that tends to win Pro Bowl votes, and it cost him recognition his production arguably earned. Jerry Rice (13 PB, 22,895 yards) remains the standard nobody else in NFL history has matched.
source: StatMuse / Pro Football Reference career Pro Bowl selections and receiving yards.

fact: Bobby Abreu and Adam Dunn each made exactly 2 All-Star teams — but Dunn hit 174 more career home runs (462 to Abreu's 288). Abreu's value came from on-base percentage, doubles, and stolen bases rather than pure power, a game sabermetricians rate highly but All-Star voters historically haven't rewarded the same way as a big home run total. Griffey (13 AS, 630 HR) and Rodriguez (14 AS, 696 HR) show what it looks like when a player's power and his recognition actually line up.
source: StatMuse career All-Star selections and home run totals.

fact: Rod Carew was an All-Star in 18 different seasons — more than George Brett (13) or Gary Sheffield (9) — and hit 92 home runs in his entire career. Sheffield hit 509. Carew's case was built almost entirely on batting average and on-base skill: he won seven batting titles and reached base constantly, which is a kind of stardom the home-run column simply doesn't record.
source: Lahman / Chadwick Bureau baseball databank (core/Batting.csv, core/AllstarFull.csv). Career regular-season totals summed by playerID; All-Star selections counted as distinct years.

fact: Ozzie Smith stole 580 bases and hit 28 home runs — for his whole career. Andre Dawson, the closest of these three in steals at 314, hit 438. Smith is the clearest case in baseball of a first-ballot Hall of Famer whose value lived almost entirely in places the box score barely tracks: defense at shortstop, and legs.
source: Lahman / Chadwick Bureau baseball databank (core/Batting.csv, core/AllstarFull.csv). Career regular-season totals summed by playerID; All-Star selections counted as distinct years.

fact: Harmon Killebrew hit 573 home runs and only 290 doubles — nearly twice as many homers as doubles, which is close to backwards for a hitter. Eddie Murray, with a similar 504 home runs, hit 560 doubles. Killebrew simply didn't hit many balls that stayed in the park: he either cleared the fence or he didn't.
source: Lahman / Chadwick Bureau baseball databank (core/Batting.csv, core/AllstarFull.csv). Career regular-season totals summed by playerID; All-Star selections counted as distinct years.

fact: Ty Cobb's .366 career batting average is the highest in major-league history, and he hit 117 home runs doing it — fewer than a quarter of Ted Williams' 521, and Williams is the one player here who did both. Cobb played nearly his whole career in the dead-ball era, when the game was built on contact, speed and place-hitting rather than power.
source: Lahman / Chadwick Bureau baseball databank (core/Batting.csv). Career regular-season totals summed by playerID; batting average computed as H/AB.

fact: Tim Raines stole 808 bases — more than four times Mike Schmidt's and Mark McGwire's combined — while hitting 170 home runs. He is second on this chart in steals and still miles behind Rickey Henderson's 1,406, which is the single most untouchable counting record in baseball. Raines waited ten years on the Hall of Fame ballot largely because the skills he was best at don't photograph well.
source: Lahman / Chadwick Bureau baseball databank (core/Batting.csv, core/AllstarFull.csv). Career regular-season totals summed by playerID; All-Star selections counted as distinct years.

fact: Babe Ruth struck out 1,330 times, which was considered reckless in his era — and it is fewer strikeouts than Willie McCovey, Reggie Jackson, or plenty of ordinary modern hitters. He hit 714 home runs against them. Reggie Jackson, the all-time strikeout leader at 2,597, needed nearly twice as many strikeouts to hit 563.
source: Lahman / Chadwick Bureau baseball databank (core/Batting.csv, core/AllstarFull.csv). Career regular-season totals summed by playerID; All-Star selections counted as distinct years.

fact: Eli Manning threw 27 interceptions and 18 touchdowns in 2013 — one of the very few modern seasons where a full-time starter finished with more interceptions than touchdown passes. Ben Roethlisberger, playing the same season, threw 28 touchdowns against 14 picks. Manning won two Super Bowl MVPs and also produced this.
source: nflverse-data player_stats release. Regular-season weekly rows aggregated by player_id and season.

fact: Devon Achane averaged 7.8 yards per carry as a rookie in 2023 — a figure that would be an all-time record over a full workload — and finished with 800 rushing yards, the fewest on this chart. He was that efficient precisely because he was used sparingly. Volume and efficiency in the running game usually pull against each other, and this is the cleanest example of it.
source: nflverse-data player_stats release. Regular-season weekly rows aggregated by player_id and season.

fact: Shaun Alexander's 2005 MVP season was 1,880 rushing yards and 78 receiving yards. Fred Taylor, with 566 fewer rushing yards, had five times the receiving production. Alexander was a pure between-the-tackles runner in an offense that never asked him to catch anything — a role that has essentially disappeared from the modern NFL.
source: nflverse-data player_stats release. Regular-season weekly rows aggregated by player_id and season.

fact: Wes Welker caught 112 passes in 2007 — the most on this chart by ten — for 1,175 yards, which is fewer than Terrell Owens gained on 35 fewer catches. That is 10.5 yards a reception against Owens' 15.6. Welker's whole game was volume underneath, and it made him one of the most productive receivers of his era without ever being a deep threat.
source: nflverse-data player_stats release. Regular-season weekly rows aggregated by player_id and season.

fact: Corey Dillon rushed for 50.8 yards a game in 2006 — the least of these four — and scored 13 rushing touchdowns, the most. Adrian Peterson needed nearly twice the yardage per game to score ten. Dillon was splitting carries with Laurence Maroney by then but kept the goal-line work, which is the single most efficient way to look productive in the column fans actually remember.
source: nflverse-data player_stats release. Regular-season weekly rows aggregated by player_id and season.

fact: Aaron Rodgers threw 45 touchdowns against 6 interceptions in 2011, a ratio of 7.5 to 1 in a season where he also posted the highest single-season passer rating in NFL history at the time. Peyton Manning's 2014 — 39 touchdowns, 15 picks — is an excellent season and is not close to this.
source: nflverse-data player_stats release. Regular-season weekly rows aggregated by player_id and season.

fact: Baron Davis took 20.9 shots a game in 2003-04 — more than anyone else here — and converted at a 49.2 true shooting percentage, the worst of the four by eight points. Aaron Gordon's 2022-23 is the mirror image: barely half the shots, and the most efficient season on the chart. Volume scoring and efficient scoring are close to opposite skills, and the box score rewards the first one.
source: stats.nba.com leaguedashplayerstats, via the sportsdataverse/hoopR nba_stats_player_season_stats release. Regular-season per-game averages.

fact: Kemba Walker scored 25.6 a game in 2018-19, the most here by two points over Karl Malone's 2000-01 — and contributed the fewest rebounds and assists of the four. Tim Duncan, ten points behind him in scoring, out-produced him everywhere else. Walker was an All-NBA guard that year on almost pure scoring volume.
source: stats.nba.com leaguedashplayerstats, via the sportsdataverse/hoopR nba_stats_player_season_stats release. Regular-season per-game averages.

fact: Jarrett Allen used 16.3% of his team's possessions in 2020-21 — the lowest share on this chart — and finished with a 66.1 true shooting percentage, the highest by ten points. That is the role-player bargain in one data point: he only ever shot when it was already a good shot. Zach Randolph used almost twice the possessions to score far less efficiently.
source: stats.nba.com leaguedashplayerstats, via the sportsdataverse/hoopR nba_stats_player_season_stats release. Regular-season per-game averages.

fact: Zion Williamson averaged 27.0 points in 2020-21 — more than Ja Morant's best scoring season here — while his rebounds and assists combined stayed at 10.9, below Bam Adebayo's 13.5 on eight fewer points a game. Williamson's production is unusually concentrated: he is one of the most efficient interior scorers on record and does comparatively little of everything else.
source: stats.nba.com leaguedashplayerstats, via the sportsdataverse/hoopR nba_stats_player_season_stats release. Regular-season per-game averages.

fact: Shawn Marion played 38.8 minutes a game in 2004-05, the most on this chart, and scored the fewest points of the four. Nikola Vučević scored more in seven fewer minutes. Marion was the defensive engine of a 62-win Suns team that ran its offense through Steve Nash and Amar'e Stoudemire — minutes measure trust, not usage.
source: stats.nba.com leaguedashplayerstats, via the sportsdataverse/hoopR nba_stats_player_season_stats release. Regular-season per-game averages.

fact: In his 2005-06 MVP-calibre season Dirk Nowitzki blocked more shots (1.0 a game) than he took steals (0.7) — the only player here that's true of, and a genuinely unusual shape for a perimeter-oriented seven-footer. Kobe Bryant, playing guard, had twice the steals and half the blocks.
source: stats.nba.com leaguedashplayerstats, via the sportsdataverse/hoopR nba_stats_player_season_stats release. Regular-season per-game averages.

fact: Chris Webber used 31.1% of Sacramento's possessions in 2000-01, the highest share here by five points, and turned them into a 51.6 true shooting percentage — the lowest. JJ Redick, at two-thirds the usage, was nine points more efficient. Usage measures how often an offense runs through you, not how well it works when it does.
source: stats.nba.com leaguedashplayerstats, via the sportsdataverse/hoopR nba_stats_player_season_stats release. Regular-season per-game averages.

fact: LaMarcus Aldridge took 19.9 shots a game in 2014-15 and posted a 52.8 true shooting percentage. LeBron James, taking two fewer shots that same era, scored at 64.9 — twelve points better. Aldridge's signature shot was the long two, the least efficient in basketball, and it is the single clearest reason the league stopped taking it.
source: stats.nba.com leaguedashplayerstats, via the sportsdataverse/hoopR nba_stats_player_season_stats release. Regular-season per-game averages.

fact: Jeff Bagwell hit 449 home runs and made four All-Star teams. Kirby Puckett, with 242 fewer homers, made ten. Bagwell won an MVP and an unanimous one at that, yet spent his career in Houston behind a wall of first basemen who were more famous than he was — All-Star voting measures how well known you are at least as much as how good.
source: Lahman / Chadwick Bureau baseball databank (core/Batting.csv, core/AllstarFull.csv). Career regular-season totals summed by playerID; All-Star selections counted as distinct years.

fact: Tony Gwynn hit .338 for his career, the highest of any player since Ted Williams retired, and hit 135 home runs doing it — fewer than a third of Andre Dawson's 438. Gwynn struck out 434 times in twenty seasons; plenty of modern hitters manage that in three. He was the last great practitioner of a style of hitting the sport has essentially stopped teaching.
source: Lahman / Chadwick Bureau baseball databank (core/Batting.csv). Career regular-season totals summed by playerID; batting average computed as H/AB.

fact: Kenny Lofton stole 622 bases — more than Mike Schmidt, Fred McGriff and Andre Dawson combined, several times over — and hit 130 home runs. He fell off the Hall of Fame ballot after a single year, which is the sort of thing that happens to players whose value came from getting on base and then running, neither of which anybody built a highlight reel around.
source: Lahman / Chadwick Bureau baseball databank (core/Batting.csv, core/AllstarFull.csv). Career regular-season totals summed by playerID; All-Star selections counted as distinct years.

fact: Mark McGwire hit 583 home runs and 252 doubles — more than twice as many homers as doubles, which is close to backwards for a hitter. Eddie Murray, with 79 fewer home runs, hit more than double the doubles. McGwire hit the ball over the fence or not at all: he also drew 1,317 walks because pitchers stopped giving him anything to hit.
source: Lahman / Chadwick Bureau baseball databank (core/Batting.csv, core/AllstarFull.csv). Career regular-season totals summed by playerID; All-Star selections counted as distinct years.

fact: Johnny Bench hit .267 with 389 home runs — the lowest average here by a distance, and more homers than George Brett and Yogi Berra. Ty Cobb, a hundred points of average higher, hit 117. Bench was the best defensive catcher who ever lived and hit like a corner slugger, which is why the batting average almost nobody remembers is the one number that looks ordinary.
source: Lahman / Chadwick Bureau baseball databank (core/Batting.csv). Career regular-season totals summed by playerID; batting average computed as H/AB.

fact: Lamar Jackson averaged 5.5 yards a carry in 2023 — well clear of Jamal Lewis and Adrian Peterson here — for 821 rushing yards, the fewest of the four. He is a quarterback: the efficiency comes from running only when the defense has already lost, and the volume stays low because running is the fallback, not the plan.
source: nflverse-data player_stats release, regular-season weekly rows aggregated by player_id and season. Season yardage is derived from play-by-play and can differ from official gamebook totals by a yard or two.

fact: Rudy Gobert took 8.1 shots a game in 2023-24 and made them at a 67.5 true shooting percentage. Allen Iverson's 2001-02 is the exact inverse: 27.8 attempts at 48.9. Gobert essentially only shoots dunks and layups created by someone else, which is why he leads the league in efficiency and why nobody has ever built an offense around him.
source: stats.nba.com leaguedashplayerstats, via the sportsdataverse/hoopR nba_stats_player_season_stats release. Regular-season per-game averages.

fact: Antawn Jamison took 22.1 shots a game in 2000-01 and posted a 49.9 true shooting percentage — the most shots here and the worst efficiency, on a Golden State team that won 17 games. Shaquille O'Neal's 2008-09, at half the volume, was 12 points more efficient. Somebody has to shoot on a bad team, and the numbers it produces look like stardom without being it.
source: stats.nba.com leaguedashplayerstats, via the sportsdataverse/hoopR nba_stats_player_season_stats release. Regular-season per-game averages.

fact: John Wall played 37.8 minutes a game as a rookie in 2010-11 — more than anyone else on this chart — and scored 16.4 points, the fewest. Lauri Markkanen scored more in six fewer minutes. Wall was the first pick on a 23-win team, which buys you every minute available and very little help scoring.
source: stats.nba.com leaguedashplayerstats, via the sportsdataverse/hoopR nba_stats_player_season_stats release. Regular-season per-game averages.

fact: Nikola Vučević used 29.2% of Orlando's possessions in 2020-21 at a 56.0 true shooting percentage. DeMar DeRozan, at 26.2% usage, was four points more efficient, and Kyle Lowry more efficient still on far fewer. High usage on a team without a better option is a description of the roster, not a measure of the player.
source: stats.nba.com leaguedashplayerstats, via the sportsdataverse/hoopR nba_stats_player_season_stats release. Regular-season per-game averages.

fact: Elton Brand played 39.3 minutes a game in 2000-01 — the most on this chart — and scored 20.1 points, the fewest. He was 22, Rookie of the Year the season before, and playing for a Chicago team that won 15 games. Minutes at that age are usually a sign nobody else on the roster can be trusted with them.
source: stats.nba.com leaguedashplayerstats, via the sportsdataverse/hoopR nba_stats_player_season_stats release. Regular-season per-game averages.

fact: Christian McCaffrey caught 116 passes in 2019 — more than Terrell Owens, Antonio Gates or Justin Jefferson in any of these seasons — for 1,005 yards, the fewest of the four. He is a running back. Jefferson needed 13 fewer catches to gain 528 more yards, because his came 15 yards downfield and McCaffrey's came at the line of scrimmage.
source: nflverse-data player_stats release, regular-season weekly rows aggregated by player_id and season. Season yardage is derived from play-by-play and can differ from official gamebook totals by a yard or two.

fact: Rob Gronkowski caught 69 passes in 2017 — the fewest here by nine — and gained 1,084 yards, the most. That is 15.7 yards a catch from a tight end, a position that exists to convert third and four. Chris Godwin needed 35 more receptions to gain 61 fewer yards.
source: nflverse-data player_stats release, regular-season weekly rows aggregated by player_id and season. Season yardage is derived from play-by-play and can differ from official gamebook totals by a yard or two.

fact: Jamaal Charles gained 94.3 rushing yards a game in 2012, the most on this chart, and scored five touchdowns. Arian Foster, five yards a game behind him, scored fifteen. Kansas City used Peyton Hillis and Shaun Draughn at the goal line, so Charles did the work that moves the ball and someone else did the work that shows up in fantasy scoring.
source: nflverse-data player_stats release, regular-season weekly rows aggregated by player_id and season. Season yardage is derived from play-by-play and can differ from official gamebook totals by a yard or two.

fact: Amon-Ra St. Brown caught 106 passes in 2022 for 1,161 yards. A.J. Brown, that same season, caught 18 fewer for 335 more. Both are excellent receivers doing entirely different jobs: one lives in the slot and moves the chains, the other runs past people. The catch column flatters the first and the yardage column flatters the second.
source: nflverse-data player_stats release, regular-season weekly rows aggregated by player_id and season. Season yardage is derived from play-by-play and can differ from official gamebook totals by a yard or two.

fact: Rachaad White gained 613 rushing yards in 2024 — the fewest here by nearly 200 — and 393 through the air, more than LeSean McCoy or Josh Jacobs managed in seasons where they ran for twice as much. Nearly 40% of White's offense came as a receiver, a split that would have been unthinkable for a starting back a generation ago.
source: nflverse-data player_stats release, regular-season weekly rows aggregated by player_id and season. Season yardage is derived from play-by-play and can differ from official gamebook totals by a yard or two.

fact: The power/contact trade-off is real, and Ted Williams mostly ignored it. He hit .344 for his career — higher than Tony Gwynn's .338, and Gwynn built a Hall of Fame case almost entirely on batting titles, finishing with 135 home runs. Williams hit 521, within 42 of Reggie Jackson, who hit .262 and struck out more times (2,597) than any batter in history. Hank Aaron (.305, 755) marks the outer edge of sustained power. And Williams did it having lost nearly five full seasons in his prime to military service in two wars.
source: StatMuse career batting average and home run totals; career strikeout leaderboard.

fact: Jamaal Charles averaged 5.4 yards per carry — the highest of any running back in NFL history with at least 1,000 attempts, ahead of Barry Sanders' 5.0 and Jim Brown's 5.2. The only players above him on the overall list are quarterbacks (Lamar Jackson, Russell Wilson, Cam Newton), who pick their runs. Charles did it on 1,407 carries, under a third of Emmitt Smith's 4,409. Smith holds the career rushing yards record and Charles holds the rate, which is a fair summary of how football remembers running backs: volume gets the record, efficiency gets forgotten.
source: StatMuse career rushing attempts and yards per carry; yards-per-carry leaderboard with a 1,000-attempt minimum.

fact: Wilt Chamberlain and Michael Jordan have the same career scoring average — 30.1 points per game, the two highest in NBA history. Their peaks are not close. Jordan's best year was 37.1 in 1986-87. Wilt's was 50.4 in 1961-62: thirteen points per game higher than the best season Jordan ever played, and nearly double Tim Duncan's career average. Kobe's 35.4 in 2005-06 is the season with the 81-point game in it, and it still doesn't reach Jordan's peak. Wilt's career average and his best season are two entirely different players.
source: StatMuse career and single-season points per game; all-time career PPG leaderboard.

fact: Power and speed almost never share a career. Mark McGwire hit 583 home runs and stole 12 bases — total, across his entire career. Rickey Henderson stole 1,406, the all-time record and about 50% more than second place, and hit 297. Ichiro (117 HR, 509 SB) is the pure contact-and-speed pole. Willie Mays hit 660 home runs *and* stole 338 bases: more power than McGwire and more steals than most players who were known for stealing. That corner of this chart is essentially empty, and it's most of why Mays is in the greatest-player-ever argument at all.
source: StatMuse career home run and stolen base totals; all-time career stolen base leaderboard.

fact: Dan Marino threw for 420 touchdowns and rushed for 87 yards. Not 87 per season — 87 total, across seventeen years. Peyton Manning managed 667 in the same number of seasons. Michael Vick rushed for 6,109, more than most of the running backs of his era and more than any quarterback in NFL history at the time he retired, while throwing 133 touchdown passes. The chart shows the trade the position used to demand: Marino and Manning bought passing volume by never leaving the pocket, and Vick bought a dimension nobody else had by never being a high-volume passer.
source: StatMuse career passing touchdowns and career rushing yards.

fact: Ichiro Suzuki collected 3,089 hits in the majors and hit 117 home runs — and he didn't play his first MLB game until he was 27. He had already recorded 1,278 hits in Japan, which puts his professional total at 4,367, more than Pete Rose's all-time MLB record of 4,256 (the combined figure isn't an official mark, since the two leagues are counted separately). Babe Ruth is the shape-inversion on this chart: 714 home runs on fewer hits than Ichiro, because a startling share of his contact left the park.
source: StatMuse career hits and home runs; NPB hit total via MLB.com and Baseball-Reference Bullpen.

fact: Almost nobody scores more in the playoffs than the regular season — the defenses tighten, the rotations shorten, and the games slow down. Larry Bird went 24.3 to 23.8. Karl Malone went 25.0 to 24.7. Allen Iverson went 26.7 to 29.7, a three-point jump, the largest of any high-volume scorer in league history. He is 6'0" and 165 pounds and never won a title, and the thing people remember — carrying a team to the Finals and stealing Game 1 from a 56-win Lakers side — is exactly what this number describes.
source: StatMuse career regular season and playoff points per game.

fact: Larry Walker hit 383 home runs and made five All-Star teams. Kirby Puckett, with 176 fewer homers, made ten. Walker won an MVP and three batting titles in Colorado, where the thin air meant voters spent two decades discounting everything he did — he waited until his final year on the ballot to reach the Hall of Fame.
source: Lahman / Chadwick Bureau baseball databank (core/Batting.csv, core/AllstarFull.csv). Career regular-season totals summed by playerID; All-Star selections counted as distinct years.

fact: Andruw Jones hit 434 home runs and made five All-Star teams — fewer than Kirby Puckett, who hit 227 fewer. Jones was also the best defensive center fielder of his generation by a wide margin, winning ten straight Gold Gloves. Neither the power nor the defense translated into the recognition either one alone usually buys.
source: Lahman / Chadwick Bureau baseball databank (core/Batting.csv, core/AllstarFull.csv). Career regular-season totals summed by playerID; All-Star selections counted as distinct years.

fact: Kirby Puckett hit .318 with 207 home runs across just twelve seasons — glaucoma ended his career at 35. Andruw Jones, sixty points of average lower, hit more than twice as many homers. Puckett is the rare modern hitter voted in almost entirely on contact and a decade of being the most beloved player in his city.
source: Lahman / Chadwick Bureau baseball databank (core/Batting.csv). Career regular-season totals summed by playerID; batting average computed as H/AB.

fact: Mike Schmidt hit 548 home runs and 408 doubles. Eddie Murray, 44 homers behind him, hit 152 more doubles. Tim Raines hit more doubles than either while hitting 170 homers total. Schmidt is generally considered the best third baseman who ever played, and the shape of his hitting — walks and homers, comparatively little in between — is the modern profile arriving forty years early.
source: Lahman / Chadwick Bureau baseball databank (core/Batting.csv, core/AllstarFull.csv). Career regular-season totals summed by playerID; All-Star selections counted as distinct years.

fact: Craig Biggio stole 414 bases and hit 291 home runs — a combination Mike Schmidt and Fred McGriff never came close to from either direction. He also caught, played second base, and played center field, and was hit by 285 pitches, second most in history. Almost nothing about his career fits a single column.
source: Lahman / Chadwick Bureau baseball databank (core/Batting.csv, core/AllstarFull.csv). Career regular-season totals summed by playerID; All-Star selections counted as distinct years.

fact: Deandre Ayton took 10.0 shots a game in 2020-21 at a 65.3 true shooting percentage — the fewest attempts here and by far the most efficient. DeMar DeRozan took nearly twice as many at ten points worse. Ayton was the fourth option on a Suns team that reached the Finals, and shooting less is a large part of why his numbers look like that.
source: stats.nba.com leaguedashplayerstats, via the sportsdataverse/hoopR nba_stats_player_season_stats release. Regular-season per-game averages.

fact: Monta Ellis took 20.1 shots a game in 2010-11 and converted at 53.6 true shooting — the most volume and the worst efficiency of the four. Joel Embiid, at 17.6 attempts, was ten points better. Ellis scored 24.1 points a game that season on a 36-win team, which is the clearest illustration there is that points per game and good offense are not the same statistic.
source: stats.nba.com leaguedashplayerstats, via the sportsdataverse/hoopR nba_stats_player_season_stats release. Regular-season per-game averages.

fact: Aaron Gordon shot 43.6% from three in 2024-25 on 3.4 attempts a game — the best percentage on this chart by five points, on the fewest attempts. Jerami Grant took nearly twice as many at seven points worse. A low-volume shooter only takes the open ones, which is exactly why the percentage looks like that and why it rarely survives more attempts.
source: stats.nba.com leaguedashplayerstats, via the sportsdataverse/hoopR nba_stats_player_season_stats release. Regular-season per-game averages.

fact: Pau Gasol played 37.0 minutes a game in 2008-09 and scored 18.9 points, the fewest here despite the second-most minutes. Anthony Davis scored seven more in three fewer. Gasol was the second option on a championship Lakers team whose first option took 20 shots a night — minutes measure how much a team needs you on the floor, not how often they throw you the ball.
source: stats.nba.com leaguedashplayerstats, via the sportsdataverse/hoopR nba_stats_player_season_stats release. Regular-season per-game averages.

fact: Le'Veon Bell gained 105.7 rushing yards a game in 2016 — the most on this chart by sixteen — and scored seven touchdowns. LaDainian Tomlinson's 2004 scored seventeen on less yardage per game. Pittsburgh used Bell to move the ball and had other answers at the goal line, so the column most people check understates the best season of his career.

fact: Calvin Johnson caught 71 passes in 2014 for 1,077 yards — 15.2 a catch, on the fewest receptions here. Chris Godwin needed 33 more catches to gain less. Johnson played only 13 games that year with an ankle injury and still finished within 30 yards of receivers who played a full season.
